dedupe_keys.name: alcacer do sal bridge rail traffic weigh in motion testbed

description: Researchers installed a rail weigh-in-motion system on the Alcácer do Sal bridge in Portugal to characterise actual train loads on an ageing railway asset. Rail-pad fibre-optic sensors measured speed and axle spacing; strain gauges estimated axle loads. The 2012–2013 campaign captured 565 trains over interrupted periods equivalent to about two months, and a labelled subset of 100 trains was used to test train-type classification methods. The Data in Brief article and its linked Zenodo data deposit are public under CC BY 4.0. This is a measurement testbed on one bridge, not an executed strengthening project or a complete year of network traffic. Collection interruptions, seasonal concentration and inferred train labels are limitations for use as a national traffic forecast. The documented outcome is a train-load and geometry dataset plus a classification procedure for future structural-load assessment. A reviewer-assessed use is calibrating bridge-fatigue traffic scenarios. G2-0620 is the related data deposit; no reusable trained classifier weights or bridge-fatigue model were verified. No measurement archive was downloaded.
name: Alcácer do Sal bridge rail-traffic weigh-in-motion testbed
notes: G2-0626. Case-study record for the documented application. Distinct from the linked data-deposit draft; publication does not prove an infrastructure intervention was implemented.
outcomes: The bridge installation recorded and processed 565 passing trains, measuring speed, axle spacing and axle loads; a 100-train labelled subset supported testing several train-type classifiers. The article presents input evidence for later fatigue assessments but does not report a completed bridge retrofit.
provider: CONSTRUCT and Faculty of Engineering, University of Porto
